matches.rationale: No finding addresses the abstract's mis-stated exponent (d^{O(1/ε)} instead of d^{O(1/ε²)}). Findings 1 and 3 discuss exponent inconsistencies between theorems but not the abstract error.

Finding 5 notes that the abstract/informal claim of lower bound exp(Ω(1/ε)) is inconsistent with the formal statement's ε^{-1/6} or ε^{-1/7}, matching the ground truth's overstatement of the lower bound.
No finding mentions the fabricated citation [ZKL23] in the Introduction.
The Bregman divergence definition reversal (swapping y and p) is not noted by any finding.
No finding mentions the claim that TreeCal does not require knowledge of ρ, while the algorithm actually depends on it.
The confusion between TreeCal being nearly identical to prior work and yet a novel analysis is not identified in any finding.
The misleading claim that the ℓ₂ calibration bound is independent of d (ignoring diameter's dimension dependence) is not detected.
No finding points to an error in the strong convexity inequality sign.
The overstatement 'completely solves the high-dimensional calibration problem' is not mentioned by any finding.
The changed constant in Theorem C.1 (3b/L to b/L) is not noted.
No finding addresses the missing funding disclosure for the Google Research affiliation.
The logical inconsistency regarding BTL's implementability and regret is not identified.
No finding discusses the misattribution of novelty for the TreeSwap-based analysis.
Finding 2 questions the inequality direction but assumes the paper has '≤'; the ground truth corruption would make it '≥', so the issue is not captured.
The overstatement about arbitrary convex sets and norms, without noting central symmetry requirements, is not flagged.
The omission of computational complexity analysis is not mentioned in any finding.
No finding points to an error in the calibration error definition (normalization by T).
Finding 5 notes an inconsistency but reports the formal statement as having exponent 1/14; the corruption that changes 1/14 to 1/7 is not detected.
